newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end lower on light foreign sales.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end lower on light foreign sales.

text.p: Thai stocks fluctuated heavily on Wednesday before ending slightly down in moderate trade on light foreign selling, especially of finance and banking issues, brokers said.
The SET index, which hit an intraday peak of 963.58, slipped 6.90 points by the close to 949.44, near the day's low. Total turnover was 5.7 billion baht.
"Foreigners continued selling today although local mutual funds entered the market and bought some stocks," said Somchai Trairattanapirom of Sitca Investment and Securities.

The banking sector fell 0.04 percent even after the Siam Commercial Bank, Thailand's fourth largest commercial bank, announced earlier in the day that its unaudited third quarter net profit would be up 17 percent over the corresponding year ago quarter at 2.33 billion baht.
Siam Commmercial Bank ended unchanged at 210 baht and ranked third on the list of most active stocks in terms of value.
"The announcement helped Siam Commercial Bank alone and didn't help the whole sector as several bank issues were sold today," Somchai said.
Thai mutual funds were cautious buyers of selected stocks, brokers said.

Several bank issues including Krung Thai Bank, Thailand's second largest commercial bank, declined one baht to 86. Siam City Bank was down 0.75 to 30 after announcing earlier today its unaudited third quarter net profit rose to 804.03 million baht from 518.07 million baht in the same period last year.
Thai Farmers Bank topped the active list in terms of value, gaining one baht to 146. Large capitalised Finance One slipped 0.50 to 84.50 and Advanced Info Service declined 10 to 324.
